views.rationale:
RECOMMENDATION: Stay at the table and close a narrow Phase One text now, conditioned on simultaneous, proportional cancellation of the December 15 List 4B tariffs and a first-step rollback of some existing additional duties. Offer agricultural purchases and already-teed-up market-access steps (poultry, selected farm exemptions, financial opening, IP/currency language already discussed) as the price of that tariff relief — not as a unilateral gift. Do not escalate rare-earths, the unreliable-entity list, or new detainee pressure while this window is open, and do not concede industrial-subsidy or Made-in-China-2025 structural reform in Phase One.

SUPPORTING RATIONALE: Threat is material but not existential. US tariffs already cover List 3 at 25% (raised 10 May 2019) and List 4A at 15% (~$110–125B, effective 1 Sep 2019), with List 4B (~phones, laptops, toys) still scheduled for 15 Dec unless a deal lands; that cliff hits China’s highest-value export basket. Huawei remains on the Entity List (16 May 2019; affiliates expanded Aug 2019; temporary general license only through 18 Nov), Meng Wanzhou is still held, and the 5 Aug currency-manipulator designation plus CNY through 7 added FX/political pressure. The real economy is already absorbing the war: Q2 GDP slowed to 6.2% (weakest in decades), industrial output hit a 17-year low of 5.0% in May, and US-bound goods exports are down more than 12% with firms shifting capacity to Vietnam/Indonesia. That maps above neutral and toward the +0.5 CHN anchor (export hit + Huawei targeting + FX), but not to +1.0: PMI returned above 50 in October, IP rebounded to 5.8% in September, Beijing still claims the 6–6.5% growth band, and net trade has not collapsed. Action should be mild-positive, not escalatory: Trump announced a Phase One outline on 11 Oct (ag purchases ~$40–50B, IP/currency cited, mid-October hike delayed), Liu He–Lighthizer/Mnuchin calls through mid-November were described as constructive, and MOFCOM (7 Nov) said both sides had agreed to remove additional tariffs in phases — even as Navarro and Trump publicly denied a commitment to lift existing levies and farm-purchase numbers remain a snag. Escalation now would likely lock in Dec 15 and deepen the Huawei/tech squeeze; a full concession (unconditional $50B purchases or structural SOE/subsidy giveaways) would spend leverage before Washington has matched on tariffs. Negotiate — lock the easy phase, insist rollback scale matches the agreement, keep Huawei/Meng and core industrial policy off this text.
key_factors: Dec 15 List 4B cliff still live on phones/laptops/toys
Existing 25% List 3 and 15% List 4A already taxing the export machine
Huawei Entity List + Meng detention remain outside the Phase One text
Growth/IP/export-hub stress is real but not a financial-stability break
Phase One is advanced enough to trade farm purchases for tariff standstill/rollback
White House is divided on rolling back existing tariffs — do not pre-concede

sources_cited.excerpt: Trump announces a Phase One deal in principle: China to buy roughly $40–50B of US agricultural products annually; IP and currency cited; planned mid-October tariff hike delayed.
US Commerce Department adds Huawei and affiliates to the Entity List. US firms generally barred from selling to Huawei without a license.
List 4A takes effect at 15% (~$110–125B of Chinese imports). China's first tranche of the ~$75B retaliation also takes effect.
After CNY breaks 7 per USD, US Treasury designates China a currency manipulator (first such designation since 1994).
MOFCOM spokesman Gao Feng: both sides agreed to remove additional tariffs in phases; if Phase One is reached, rollbacks should be simultaneous and in the same proportion. Signing this month unlikely.
US official said rollback would be part of Phase One; Peter Navarro denied any agreement to remove existing tariffs. Dec 15 ~$156B list still the expected first US concession if a deal is signed.

16 Nov Liu He call with Mnuchin/Lighthizer described as constructive; talks had hit a snag over farm-purchase amounts and IP/tech-transfer versus tariff rollback. Trump has not agreed to lift existing levies.
China's goods exports to the US down more than 12% this year; industrial output growth fell to a 17-year low in summer; manufacturers relocating to Vietnam/Indonesia.
Huawei status was not part of the October Phase One outline; Lighthizer said the president had not made a final decision on the Dec 15 tariffs.
